reply: I like to eat a healthy breakfast every morning.
translation: मुझे हर सुबह एक स्वस्थ नाश्ता करना पसंद है।
reason: In Hindi, 'to like to do something' is often expressed using 'करना पसंद है' (karna pasand hai). For meals like breakfast, 'करना' (to do/have) is sometimes used instead of 'खाना' (to eat) for a more natural flow.

reply: Do you want to eat out tonight or cook at home?
translation: क्या आप आज रात बाहर खाना चाहते हैं या घर पर खाना बनाना चाहते हैं?
reason: 'चाहते हैं?' (chahte hain?) is used to ask 'Do you want to?'. 'बाहर खाना' (bahar khaana) directly translates to 'to eat out', and 'खाना बनाना' (khaana banaana) means 'to cook food'.

reply: It's important to eat your vegetables for good health.
translation: अच्छे स्वास्थ्य के लिए अपनी सब्जियां खाना महत्वपूर्ण है।
reason: The infinitive verb 'खाना' (khaana - to eat) functions as a gerund (eating) in this context. 'के लिए' (ke liye) means 'for', indicating purpose.

reply: The children were told not to eat too many sweets before dinner.
translation: बच्चों को रात के खाने से पहले ज़्यादा मिठाइयाँ न खाने के लिए कहा गया था।
reason: 'न खाने के लिए कहा गया था' (na khaane ke liye kaha gaya tha) is the common way to say 'were told not to eat'. 'ज़्यादा' (zyada) means 'too many' or 'too much', and 'से पहले' (se pehle) means 'before'.

reply: She watched the squirrel eat a nut on the park bench.
translation: उसने पार्क की बेंच पर गिलहरी को एक अखरोट खाते हुए देखा।
reason: When observing a continuous action, the present participle 'खाते हुए' (khaate hue - eating/while eating) is used with the verb 'देखा' (dekha - watched). The postposition 'को' (ko) is often used with living direct objects in Hindi.
